% Pattern: proof/environment/wrapper. A proof environment declared with an
% optional first argument, as \newenvironment{Proof}[1][Proof]{\begin{proof}[#1]},
% whose use gives the head as that argument. The head names a lemma that is
% not the item just before the proof. The second use gives no head.
% Seen in the gold pilot (set E).
% want lemma-1 statement/lemma 1 status=here labels=gap
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 2 status=none labels=main
% want proof-1 proof - proves=lemma-1
% want theorem-2 statement/theorem 3 status=here
% want proof-2 proof - proves=theorem-2
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\newenvironment{Proof}[1][Proof]{\begin{proof}[#1]}{\end{proof}}
\begin{document}
\begin{lemma}\label{gap}
A helper.
\end{lemma}
Some text between.

\begin{theorem}\label{main}
A statement.
\end{theorem}
Some more text.

\begin{Proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{gap}]
A step.
\end{Proof}
\begin{theorem}
Another statement.
\end{theorem}
\begin{Proof}
By Lemma~\ref{gap}, we are done.
\end{Proof}
\end{document}
